Subject: Re: Private cutover — intermittent egress failures

Hi Naomi,

We cut over to the private VPC link to Redwood last night (cutover window 02:00–03:00 UTC). Since then we've seen intermittent outbound failures to several external services (S3 endpoints, third-party APIs) originating from a subset of hosts in our app fleet. Failures show up as TCP resets or packets dropped; examples attached.

Symptoms:
- 10–20% of flows from app-outbound (10.50.0.0/22) to internet destinations fail intermittently.
- FW counters show rp_filter drops incrementing on our on-prem firewall for the affected subnets.
- Sample traceroutes and packet captures attached (pcap-sample-1.zip, route-snapshot.txt).

We've temporarily opened wide NAT ports on the firewall and saw transient improvement, but drops returned under burst traffic. Could this be an rp_filter false positive triggered by asymmetric return paths after the cutover?

Looking for urgent triage and a recommended remediation path (temporary and long-term).

Thanks,

Thanks Naomi — quick triage from our side after looking at the PCAP and route snapshot. Key findings so far:

- The PCAP shows TCP SYNs leaving our NAT, replies coming back on a different IP on Bluecrest's edge (asymmetric return).
- Bluecrest's firewall is configured with strict rp_filter (strict mode), which will drop packets that don't match reverse path checks.
- On our edge we are announcing prefixes via the new private path and also via legacy internet transit during the cutover — some flows are returning via the legacy path.

Immediate mitigations to request from Bluecrest (short-term):
1) Put their firewall rp_filter in loose mode for the affected subnets while we stabilize (instructions below).
2) Add a static route for the app subnet to force return via the private link if possible (route-snapshot shows the next-hop options).
3) Provide us with a short timeframe when they can toggle these safely (we want to observe counters).

If they prefer we can also revert the cutover for a short window; that's a service action and requires coordination (estimated 20–30 mins).

Jonas/Karthik — can one of you confirm whether our edge is doing any source NAT changes or influencing return path selection? Also check our BGP local preference during the cutover.

Marissa Cole
Network Reliability — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

--- Inline from PCAP ---
TCP SYN from 10.50.1.12 -> 204.79.197.200 seen on egress interface ge-0/1. Reply arrives at Bluecrest edge with source 198.51.100.14 but next-hop to 10.50.1.12 differs from what strict rp_filter expects.

Marissa, Naomi — thanks for the quick analysis. We toggled rp_filter to loose for the affected subnet and ran traceroutes. Counters on our ASA show rp_filter drops decreasing while loose mode is enabled.

Traceroute outputs (attached fw-counters.txt) show two distinct return nexthops depending on destination — one via the private Redwood peer, one via legacy transit. We also saw NAT port churn on the firewall during spikes; firewall ephemeral exhaustion may be compounding the issue.

We attached fw-counters.txt for your review. Long-term we'd prefer not to leave rp_filter loose; we want a network configuration that preserves strict filtering but avoids false positives. Please advise recommended config changes on either side (routing preferrence / BGP localpref / static host routes / NAT behavior).

Subject: RE: Fwd: Private cutover — intermittent egress failures (root cause and remediation)

Alex — thanks for the captures and counters. Wrapping up root cause and recommended actions below.

Root cause (summary):
- The cutover introduced an alternate egress path that changed return nexthop behavior for a subset of destinations. Bluecrest's firewall is running strict reverse-path-filtering; with asymmetric egress/ingress the firewall correctly dropped return packets that arrived on an interface that didn't match the routing table for the source IP.
- During burst traffic the firewall's NAT ephemeral port pool was very active; in a few spots we observed port exhaustion/reuse leading to TCP resets which magnified perceived failures.

Short-term (safe, low-risk):
- Keep rp_filter in loose mode for the affected subnets until we complete routing stabilization (monitor for 24–48h).
- Add specific /32 host routes for high-volume VIPs to force symmetric return across the private link.
- Increase firewall ephemeral port range or tune timeout to reduce port churn.

Medium-term (preferred):
- On Redwood side: prefer the private path via BGP localpref adjustments for the announced prefixes to reduce dual-path returns during cutover windows. We'll prepare a config snippet for your BGP team.
- On Bluecrest side: consider setting rp_filter to loose (1) system-wide but enable strict (2) on customer-facing interfaces where paths are known symmetric; alternatively, implement asymmetry-aware rules for the app subnets.

Long-term (prevent recurrence):
- Update our cutover playbook to include a pre-cutover BGP localpref alignment step and a post-cutover validation runbook (traceroute + fw counter checks).
- Add monitoring alert for ephemeral port saturation on customer firewalls as part of cutover checklist.

Attachments: remediation-playbook.pdf (playbook snippet + BGP localpref example). I'm also creating JIRA NETOPS-9172 to track the follow-ups (link below).

Next steps / owners:
- Bluecrest: implement short-term loose-rpfilter and add host routes (Alex) — target: 2026-12-01 20:00 UTC.
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare BGP localpref diff and confirm it with operations — target: 2026-12-02 02:00 UTC.
- Redwood (Jonas): validation script to run traceroutes and verify fw counter deltas — target: 2026-12-02 06:00 UTC.

Once Bluecrest confirms counters steady for 24h we can move rp_filter back to strict and mark stable.

Thanks — Karthik
